fair_value_policy: Fair Value V2.1 is the sole valuation baseline. Semantic scores in this file must not directly overwrite official numeric macro series or Fair Value.
summary: Four material changes since the prior snapshot: U.S. initial jobless claims fell to 196,000 for the week ended September 12; Saudi East-West Pipeline damage is now reported at three pumping stations with some sources estimating five to six weeks for full repairs; Russia's roughly 300,000-bpd Yaroslavl refinery halted crude processing after a Ukrainian drone strike; and the U.S. House passed a broad Russia/Iran sanctions bill that could authorize tariffs up to 100% on buyers of Russian energy if enacted and implemented. Hormuz physical shipping impairment remains severe, while Saudi Oman routing has kept crude prices below recent peaks.

macro_summary.taiwan_equity_implication: Lower U.S. claims reinforce labor-market resilience after the Fed hike and therefore do not provide a dovish offset for Taiwan growth equities. Taiwan's rate hold remains supportive domestically, but persistent Middle East and Russian energy disruptions, possible secondary tariff escalation, high U.S. rates and dollar strength remain major valuation, input-cost and global-demand risks.
macro_summary.notes: Official numeric series remain authoritative. Reuters market observations and semantic scores are research evidence only. No semantic score directly changes official series or Fair Value.

key_drivers.name: U.S. initial claims fall to 196,000
key_drivers.observed: U.S. Labor Department data reported by Reuters showed seasonally adjusted initial claims fell 10,000 to 196,000 in the week ended September 12 from 206,000.
key_drivers.interpretation: Labor demand remains resilient after the Fed's September hike, limiting near-term evidence for a dovish reversal. Holiday timing may have amplified weekly volatility.

key_drivers.name: Saudi East-West Pipeline damage worse than previously reported
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported three pumping stations were damaged, versus two previously reported, and cited sources estimating five to six weeks for full repairs while partial flows may resume sooner.
key_drivers.interpretation: Persistence of the Saudi Hormuz-bypass impairment is materially higher than the prior snapshot implied; Oman routing remains only a partial mitigation.

key_drivers.name: Large Russian refinery halts crude processing
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported the roughly 300,000-bpd Yaroslavl refinery halted crude processing after AVT-3 was damaged; another major primary unit was already under repair from an earlier strike.
key_drivers.interpretation: Adds persistence to global diesel/jet-fuel tightness and freight-cost pressure.

key_drivers.name: U.S. Russia/Iran sanctions bill advances to President
key_drivers.observed: The U.S. House passed the bill 262-159 after Senate passage. Reuters reports it targets Russian energy/defense and sanctions-evasion tankers and can authorize tariffs up to 100% on buyers of Russian energy.
key_drivers.interpretation: Potentially large oil/trade/global-growth shock, but implementation remains conditional because presidential approval and use of tariff authority are pending.

key_risks: Fed tightening plus resilient U.S. labor data can keep front-end yields and equity discount rates elevated.
Hormuz traffic remains severely impaired while Saudi East-West Pipeline damage now appears more persistent.
Russian refinery outages and export restrictions sustain diesel and jet-fuel scarcity.
Pending U.S. sanctions legislation could create secondary tariff exposure for China and India and disrupt energy/trade flows if enacted and implemented.
VIX, copper, USD/TWD and exact Treasury closes remain stale in this semantic snapshot.

policy_tone.fed: Hawkish tightening: target range 3.75%-4.00%; resilient claims do not provide a clear dovish offset.
policy_tone.taiwan_central_bank: Hold with selective credit easing: policy rate remains 2.0%; second-home maximum LTV is 70% from September 18.
policy_tone.china: No new official macro or monetary-policy release incorporated.
policy_tone.global: Energy shock remains inflationary and growth-negative; prospective Russia/Iran sanctions add conditional tariff and trade risk.
